coverage.note: A mutant sending retire after the terminal frame passes every test: the consumer usually reads both frames in one chunk, the 25 ms idle poll retires shortly after, and the carrier places its next call 1 s later. On a split read one call could land on a worker above its watermark; it still gets a correct result and the worker retires after it, so the main I10 clause (no idle worker kept warm above it) holds. Advisory (REV-4 weak). Owner: docs/backlog/distribution/isolate-host-retire-before-terminal-uncarried.md; ADR-0563 §Corrections residual line (2026-11-19, residual at landing).

findings.summary: The retire-before-terminal order has no discriminating carrier (the I10 sub-clause "takes no new call"). Advisory, not a residual: if it broke, one call placed in a split-read window would run on a worker above its watermark with a correct result, and the worker would retire after it. Owned by the backlog item and the ADR-0563 §Corrections residual line.

findings.summary: "every worker but one warm idle one holds at least one unsettled call" is false for up to ~1 s after deadlines. A worker whose calls all timed out and keep running is held by settled (cancelled) calls until their terminal frame, or until retire after the 1 s grace. Example: 8 stuck calls on 2 workers time out together, so 0 calls are in flight but 2 workers stay up for about 1 s, against a stated bound of 1. For RSS sizing, count cancelled isolates still running as in flight, or add "+ workers in their 1 s stuck grace".
